language.title: Language
language.intro: The language of the interface. By default Moss365 follows the display language of Windows; if that language is not available, English. Your choice here is for your Windows account on this PC and wins over the system language.
language.notdata: Names from AD and Microsoft 365 (groups, departments, policies) and the content of scripts are not translated: that is the data of the organisation.
language.partial: Not every screen is translated yet; what is missing is shown in Dutch for now and follows in the next versions.
language.applied: The language is changed; the screens are reloaded.

plan.intro: Tick what must happen. Nothing changes until Run and a confirmation. Everything goes to the change log.
plan.exchange: Exchange uses the same sign-in; if a sign-in link appears at the top, copy it to your browser.
plan.large: Yes, I checked that these {0} changes are right
plan.rereading: The objects involved are being read again (see the bottom of the menu); the page updates itself.
plan.reread: The objects involved were read again, or are marked as "changed, not yet refreshed".

start.intro: Moss365 (The Moss Directory) manages users, groups and rooms in {0}. The app starts with the inventory of Export-Inventaris.ps1 (per file the newest folder). Through Connections you load live data from {0}. Changes always happen as a plan: first a preview, then confirm, then run, and everything goes to the change log.
start.noinventory: No inventory in this tenant yet. Load live through Connections, or read below the folder that Export-Inventaris.ps1 made.
start.folder.placeholder: Full path to a folder of Export-Inventaris.ps1
start.accounts.help: "AD + Entra" are synchronised accounts. "Alleen Entra" are mostly the accounts behind shared, room and scheduling mailboxes. "Alleen AD" are disabled, technical and unsynchronised accounts.
start.departments: {0} departments, of which {1} without a division yet.
nested-groups.only-direct-memberships-no: Only direct memberships; no groups in groups.
suggestions-panel.load-data-first-connec: Load data first (Connections): the suggestions come from the accounts, groups and licences.
suggestions-panel.nothing-to-suggest-wha: Nothing to suggest: what is in the data is also under Organisation.
suggestions-panel.found-in-the-loaded-da: Found in the loaded data, not yet under Organisation. Tick what you want to take over; you can change everything afterwards.
suggestions-panel.the-app-suggests-emerg: The app suggests emergency accounts once the admin roles are loaded (Load everything live).
ca-user-card.no-entra-account-conditiona: No Entra account: Conditional Access only applies when signing in to Entra.
ca-user-card.what-if-this-person-signs: What if this person signs in...
absence.forwardend: The end of the forwarding is ready under Scheduled on {0}.
bulk.offboarding: One scheduled offboarding per person, with the default options. At the moment itself every plan is ready under Scheduled; nothing happens without confirmation. Guest users are skipped.
library.intro: New and changed scripts from the library of Moss365 (scripts/ in the repository), without updating the app. Every script is checked against its fingerprint in the index; a script that does not match is refused. A downloaded script never runs by itself. A pinned script stays at its version in {0}.
library-panel.the-library-is-up-to: The library is up to date: nothing new or changed.
absence-card.until-empty-until-you-turn: Until (empty = until you turn it off)
absence-card.keep-a-copy-in-the: Keep a copy in the mailbox
helpdesk.no-ad-account-you-set: No AD account. You set the password of a cloud account in the Entra portal (Users > Reset password).
helpdesk.the-user-must-change-it: The user must change it at the next sign-in
helpdesk.pass-the-password-on-by: Pass the password on by voice or through a separate channel, never in the same mail as the user name. The app stores it nowhere; after leaving this page it is gone. With Entra Connect it is active in Microsoft 365 within a few minutes.
helpdesk.for-someone-who-lost-their: For someone who lost their phone or still has to register MFA: a temporary code to sign in (and set up MFA again).
helpdesk.where-does-the-lockout-come: Where does the lockout come from?
helpdesk.script-reads-the-events-of: (script; reads the events of the domain controllers)
message-trace-card.did-the-mail-arrive-a: Did the mail arrive, and if not, why? Exchange Online shows the last 10 days. Every lookup goes to the access log.
message-trace-card.subject: Subject
kb-table.all-filtered-rows-with-the: All (filtered) rows, with the visible columns, in this order and sorting, as CSV for Excel
kb-table.you-can-also-drag-columns: You can also drag columns in the header of the table.
kb-table.choose-all-rows-on-this: Choose all rows on this page
variables-editor.help: The name is the parameter in the script ($Naam): only letters, digits and _. A date can also be relative, e.g. @werkjaar.van or @vorigemaand.tot.
script-result.the-script-returned-no-obj: The script returned no objects and made no CSV file.
script-result.the-script-put-no-files: The script put no files in its output folder.
script-run-panel.this-script-really-chan: This script really changes things. Sure?
script-run-panel.this-script-changes-som: This script changes something: look at the preview first. Then you can run it.
security-card.unknown-load-live-connecti: unknown (load live: Connections, Load everything live)
variables-editor.name: Name
variables-editor.question: Question
encryption.off: Off. The database holds personal data and the history of the organisation. Encrypting (AES-256, SQLCipher) protects it against a stolen disk or another user of this PC.
encryption.newkey: New recovery key: write it down or print it and keep it in a safe place (a safe):
encryption.recovery: Recovery key. Whoever forgets the password, is another Windows user or is no longer in the group, can only open the database with this key. You also restore a backup on another PC with it. Moss365 stores it nowhere: write it down or print it and keep it in a safe place (a safe).
encryption.decrypt: Store the database of {0} unencrypted again?
update.stable: Stable: only the versions after a complete step
update.preview: Preview: also the preliminary versions (0.17.0-preview.1), to test in advance
update.notinstalled: This copy was not installed with Moss365.Desktop-stable-Setup.exe (for example started from the zip), so it cannot update itself. Install with the Setup.exe of the latest release: without admin rights, and your data stays where it is.
job-profile-editor.intro: What someone gets in a job: groups, shared mailboxes, licences and details such as job title and department. You choose a profile under New user, and under Job profiles you apply it to existing users and see who has more or less. Groups and mailboxes are by name, so that a profile also works in another tenant (export and import under Company and naming). A saved profile that changes gets a new version.
encryption-panel.encrypting-is-only-poss: Encrypting is only possible in the Windows app.
encryption-panel.a-backup-is-encrypted-w: A backup is encrypted with the same key; restoring asks for the recovery key.
encryption-panel.type-the-last-group-of: Type the last group of the key to confirm
encryption-panel.last-group-of-the-recov: Last group of the recovery key
encryption-panel.the-app-makes-an-encryp: The app makes an encrypted copy, checks it and then replaces the database. The copies from before an update are removed (they are not encrypted). Backups made earlier stay unencrypted.
encryption-panel.a-new-key-for-example: A new key, for example when someone else may know the recovery key. The old recovery key no longer works afterwards (not for older backups either: those only open with the old one).
update-panel.updating-is-only-possible-i: Updating is only possible in the Windows app.
update-panel.own-source-shared-folder-wi: Own source (shared folder with the releases, empty = GitHub)
update-panel.until-1-0-every-installatio: Until 1.0 every installation follows the Preview channel by default. Going from Preview to Stable can put back an older version; it then says so.
update-panel.no-previous-version-in-this: No previous version in this channel.
update-panel.before-installing-the-app-m: Before installing, the app makes a copy of every database; then Moss365 closes and restarts.
job-profile-editor.the-app-never-gives-d: The app never gives dynamic and privileged groups through a profile. Do not forget to save (at the top).
manage-ca.intro: Every change first shows a preview; only after your confirmation does it go to Entra, and it goes to the change log (can be undone). Your own account needs the role Conditional Access Administrator (or Security Administrator), and the app registration the permission Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess (Set up tenant takes care of that).
manage-ca.reportfirst: You let a new policy run in report only first (suggestion: 14 days) and look at the effect (Policies > Load effect). Only then do you turn it on.
manage-ca.effectviewed: I looked at the effect in report only and want to turn on a policy
manage-ca.exclude: Exclude someone from a policy for a while (e.g. travelling outside the allowed countries), with an end date. On that date putting it back is ready under Scheduled; the app does not run it by itself.
manage-ca.templates: A new policy from the recommendations of Microsoft. It always starts in report only, with the emergency accounts excluded. With a pilot group it first applies only to that group. Rather do it all yourself? Make a policy in the editor, or open a policy and choose Make a copy.
manage-ca.locations: IP addresses of the buildings (CIDR, e.g. 203.0.113.10/32) or countries (two-letter code, e.g. BE), one per line. You use a trusted location with IP addresses for "register only from the office".
manage-ca.backups: After every live load the app keeps a copy of all policies and locations, if something changed. They are in the database of {0}; they hold ids of people and groups: keep them local and put a copy in a place with limited access.
manage-ca.no-backups-yet-load-live: No backups yet. Load live (Connections) or choose "Make a backup now".
manage-ca.no-differences-the-policies-ar: No differences: the policies are now as in this backup.
manage-ca.new-since-the-backup-turn: new since the backup; turn off under On and off
manage-ca.from-the-audit-log-of: From the audit log of Entra: who created, changed or deleted which policy or location (the last 30 days).
tenant-compare.none: There is no other tenant to compare with. Add one under Tenants.
rooms.intro: {0} meeting rooms from {1}. For current values: Load rooms from Exchange. Marked = differs from the standard of the organisation.
rooms.none: No rooms loaded. Load them from Exchange or from an inventory with exo-rooms-overzicht.csv.
about.releases: Every version is a release on GitHub: Moss365.Desktop-stable-Setup.exe (installs for your account and updates itself) and a zip. Your data is kept separately in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Moss365 and stays.
mailboxes.intro: Access should go through the group SG-SM-<address>-Full (FullAccess and SendAs); you clean up direct permissions on people from the page of the mailbox. Current values, also forwarding and automatic reply: Load mailboxes from Exchange.
mirror.intro: Choose a reference user (the mirror) and a target user. The app shows per group{0} what would have to happen and by which route. With Make plan you first see the changes; nothing happens until you confirm. Privileged and dynamic groups are never copied.
mirror.both: , in AD and in the cloud,
new-mailbox.intro: The plan creates the mailbox (without a licence), then the access group SG-SM-<address>-Full, gives that group FullAccess and SendAs and makes the chosen people members. If a step fails, the steps waiting for it are skipped.
script-run-detail.start-again-with-the-s: Start again with the same values
script-run-detail.the-script-of-this-one: The script of this one-off run
groups.all-groups-from-ad-entra: All groups from AD, Entra and Exchange. A group synchronised from AD is listed once, with its AD and cloud side together.
groups.all-groups-from-entra-and: All groups from Entra and Exchange.
rooms.leave-empty-do-not-change: Leave empty = do not change. Only what differs from the current value goes into the plan.
guest-renewal.every-guest-has-a-sponsor: Every guest has a sponsor who confirms each year that the guest is still needed. Otherwise guests stay forever. Asking the sponsors is a plan of mails; whoever is no longer needed, you disable (also a plan, can be undone).
about-and-updates.search-for-a-new-versi: Search for a new version at start
mirror.reference-and-target-are-the: Reference and target are the same user.
this-computer.versions: The version of Moss365 and the updates are under Version and updates.
collaboration.sharing: Sharing with people outside the organisation:
cleanup.intro: Accounts that have not signed in for a long time, to check. Tick what may go: employees are disabled (with the reason in the description, never deleted; for a full offboarding you use Offboarding), guests are deleted. After running, the app keeps a report with every account checked and the decision, as evidence of the check. Last sign-in: {0}.
cleanup.last.both: the most recent from AD and Entra
cleanup.notlive: The data is not live. Load live first, so that the last sign-ins are right.
follow-up.intro: Steps that wait until a new user exists in Entra (licence, cloud groups). Entra Connect synchronises every 30 minutes by default. Finish first checks whether the user is already there and then runs the remaining steps; they were already in the preview at creation.
follow-up.confirm: Run {0} change(s) when the user exists in Entra?
scripts-overview.scripts-only-run-in-the: Scripts only run in the Windows app (with PowerShell). Here you can look at them.
this-computer.checks-whether-everything-: Checks whether everything the app and the scripts need is present: PowerShell, the modules (in Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7 separately, since each has its own modules), the clock, the connection to the domain controller and to Microsoft 365. If something is missing, you can install it here, only from official sources (PowerShell Gallery, winget, Windows) and always after confirmation; every installation goes to the change log. Installing modules for your account needs no admin rights; PowerShell 7 and the AD module (RSAT) do: Windows then asks for confirmation.
this-computer.this-check-only-works-in: This check only works in the Windows app.
this-computer.suggest-missing-parts-righ: Suggest missing parts right after the check (the app asks once)
collaboration.microsoft-365-groups-and-t: Microsoft 365 groups and Teams without an owner, with guests or no longer used, and SharePoint sites with their storage. The activity comes from the usage reports of Microsoft 365 (up to 180 days back).
collaboration.owners-and-activity-are-ad: Owners and activity are added after "Read Teams and SharePoint".
guests.external-users-b2b-guests-in: External users (B2B guests) in Entra. Inviting and deleting go, like every change, through a plan with confirmation. A deleted guest stays 30 days under the deleted users in Entra and can be restored there.
new-group.choose-the-kind-first-it: Choose the kind first: it decides where the group goes. The plan creates the group and then the manager or owner and the first members. If creating fails, those steps are skipped.
start-script.at-the-moment-itself-a: At the moment itself a message appears (menu Actions > Scheduled) and you start the run; the app never runs anything by itself. The values come from the form above; a relative date (e.g. start of the working year) is recalculated at every run.
security-checks.health: AD health (domain controllers, replication, FSMO roles, time): start the script AD health.
edit-script.builtin: You do not change a built-in script: this is a copy of {0}. On Save it becomes an own script.
offboarding.moved: The account is disabled and moved to {0}, never deleted.
offboarding.scheduled: At the chosen moment the offboarding is ready under Scheduled. The app then calculates the plan again from the data of that moment (load live first) and runs nothing without your confirmation.
keys.search-for-a-device-the: Search for a device (the name, or part of it) or give the key ID that BitLocker shows. Every time you view a key or a password goes to the access log (who, when, which device). The app stores nothing.
keys.name-of-the-device-e: name of the device, e.g. PC-0123
keys.key-id-the-first-8: key ID (the first 8 characters are enough)
security-checks.what-an-attacker-looks-f: What an attacker looks for first, and what changed, also outside Moss365. Every check only reads; what you want to change, you do on its own screen (as a plan). A check says OK, attention or problem, and "unknown" when the data is not enough.
password-expiry.accounts-in-ad-whose-pas: Accounts in AD whose password expires soon (enabled, not "never expires"). Above all for people who are rarely on the network (home working, VPN): send a reminder, as a plan as always.
password-expiry.fill-in-after-how-many: Fill in after how many days a password expires (the password policy of the domain); 0 = does not expire.
edit-script.this-script-was-changed-outs: This script was changed outside the app since it was last saved. Check it; Save approves this version.
edit-script.this-script-changes-somethin: This script changes something (then first a preview with -WhatIf)
edit-script.what-the-form-asks-at: What the form asks at start; the app passes them as parameters to the script and remembers the last values used.
offboarding.the-account-is-disabled-sign: The account is disabled (sign-in blocked), never deleted.
offboarding.put-the-date-in-the: Put the date in the description
offboarding.convert-mailbox-to-a-shared: Convert mailbox to a shared mailbox
offboarding.run-later-e-g-on: Run later (e.g. on the last working day)
devices.computers-in-ad-that-no: Computers in AD that no longer sign in, which systems run, and devices in Intune that are not compliant or no longer seen. Disabling old computers is a plan as always; nothing is deleted.
job-profiles.intro: Choose a profile: you see who has it (received through the app, or with the same job title) and who has more or less than the profile. Applying is a plan as always: first a preview, then confirm. What someone has more, the app only suggests (not ticked). You make the profiles themselves under Settings > Organisation > Job profiles.
job-profiles.none: There are no job profiles yet. Make one under Organisation, e.g. from a user who already has the job.
security.nodata: No security data yet. Choose Load everything live or Load live (AD and Entra) on Connections; the step "Read security" fetches MFA and admin roles. For that your account needs the role Reports Reader, Security Reader or Global Reader, and the tenant Entra ID P1 (part of Business Premium).
change-log.intro: Every change run in {0}: who, when, what and with which result. Passwords are never in it.
change-log.undo.help: Tick the changes you want to undo, or choose a whole plan. The app makes the reverse plan (in reverse order) and shows it first; only after Run and a confirmation does anything change. Creating, passwords, licences and deleted guests cannot be undone.
change-log.retention: The change log stays {0} year(s) in the database (to agree with the DPO; to change under Database, where you also clean up the rest of the database). You first archive older lines to a CSV; only then can you remove them from the database.
licences.apply: You apply and clean up under Job profiles.
scheduled.intro: Offboarding and onboarding, scripts and the end of a temporary exception to a Conditional Access policy, set up for later. The app runs nothing by itself: when the moment has passed, the action is ready here and a message appears at the bottom of the menu. Choose Show plan, check it and run it. An offboarding is then calculated again from the data of that moment; so load live first.
scheduled.notlive: The data is not live. Load live first, so that the plan matches the current state.
scheduled.none: Nothing scheduled. You schedule under Offboarding, New user or Scripts.
job-profiles.also-suggest-removing-what-: Also suggest removing what is extra (not ticked)
security.unknown-the-mfa-registrations-c: Unknown: the MFA registrations could not be read.
security.active-role-assignments-who-is: Active role assignments. Who is only eligible through PIM (not yet activated) is not listed here.
change-log.filter-on-name-group-action: Filter on name, group, action or result
change-log.who-exported-and-who-viewed: Who exported and who viewed sign-ins or security data (the last 200). Only what and how much, never the content.
licences.fill-in-the-price-per: Fill in the price per month per licence: then you see what Microsoft 365 costs, per department and per division, and what you can save. Removing licences is a plan as always.
licences.no-licence-data-loaded-load: No licence data loaded: load Entra live (Connections).
scheduled.pass-this-on-to-the: Pass this on to the user; it must be changed at the first sign-in. The app stores it nowhere.
ca-policy-detail.reportonly: · report only: Entra measures what this policy would do, but enforces nothing.
history.intro: Every read (live or an inventory read in) is a snapshot in the database of {0}. The app keeps only what changed, so that you can see what the organisation looked like on every date and what changed between two dates, also what happened outside Moss365.
history.none: No snapshots yet. Load live through Connections: every read becomes one.
history.showing: All screens now show the state of {0} (read only).
database.intro: Everything of {0} is in one database ({1}, {2}). Cleaning up always first shows what would go; the change log and the access log first go to a CSV. You make a full copy under Tenants (Backup).
database.confirm: Clean up {0} part(s) in {1}? This cannot be undone (the archives stay).
ca-policy-detail.people-with-an-entra-ac: People with an Entra account for whom the part "who" matches; whether the policy really plays a part at a sign-in also depends on the app and the conditions.
ca-policy-detail.json-as-entra-gives-the: JSON as Entra gives the policy
ca-policy-detail.would-have-asked-for-an: Would have asked for an extra step
organisation-history.the-screens-then-sh: The screens then show the last snapshot from before the end of that day. Plans are not possible then.
organisation-history.that-way-a-kpi-adde: That way a KPI added later also gets its trend back, for every day with a snapshot.
database-maintenance.default-choice-u9-s: Default (choice U9): snapshots daily for a year, then one per month; change log 5 years; technical log 90 days; script runs a year.
database-maintenance.you-are-looking-at-: You are looking at a state from the past. Go back to now to clean up.
database-maintenance.nothing-is-older-th: Nothing is older than the retention periods.
logon-scripts.every-logon-script-exists-: Every logon script exists, and every script is used.
logon-scripts.they-can-still-be-started: They can still be started by another script or a group policy.
logon-scripts.scripts-that-a-group-polic: Scripts that a group policy (GPO) assigns. The app shows them but does not change them: that happens in Group Policy Management.
logon-scripts.put-the-version-from-befor: Put the version from before in the editor
statistics.history: After every live load the app keeps the state of the day (only numbers, no names); if a day is missing, History calculates it again from the snapshots. Every KPI has its own scale.
reports.title: Report {0}
group-detail.noentra: Fill in the Entra details first (Connections).
requests.request-a-new-colleague-or: Request a new colleague or a departure, without e-mails. The administrator approves or rejects; after approval the plan follows from the job profile, on the known screens. Every decision goes to the change log.
group-detail.assigns-a-licence-to-the: Assigns a licence to the members
group-detail.dynamic-group-the-members-f: Dynamic group: the members follow from the rule. Change the details of the user (e.g. office or department) instead of the group.
group-detail.this-group-is-not-a: This group is not a member of other groups.
group-detail.no-fullaccess-or-sendas-on: No FullAccess or SendAs on shared mailboxes.
statistics.shared-mailboxes-rooms-and-sc: Shared mailboxes, rooms and scheduling mailboxes also have an account, but nobody signs in with it. They do not count for the employees, the sign-ins and MFA.
statistics.signals-to-check-not-conclusi: Signals to check, not conclusions. Active accounts.
statistics.mfa-registrations-not-loaded-: MFA registrations not loaded yet: everything is unknown.
statistics.mfa-and-admin-roles-are: MFA and admin roles are not loaded yet (Connections, Load everything live).
statistics.not-loaded-yet-or-not: Not loaded yet or not readable.
reports.a-report-per-month-or: A report per month or quarter for management and information security: the indicators with their trend, the changes from the change log, data quality and the checks against the standards. Everything comes from the stored history of this tenant, so also for a period in the past.
reports.the-checks-are-evidence-for: The checks are evidence for the measures; they do not replace policy or an audit.
reports.per-department-how-many-active: Per department: how many active employees have a job title, office, manager and phone. Good data makes dynamic groups and the address book reliable.
setup.intro: The app looks for what it can find itself and shows what is missing. What it has to create or change in Entra (the app registration {0}, consent, the profiles and their groups) is first a plan below; nothing happens until you confirm, and everything goes to the change log of {1}.
setup.domain: This PC belongs to the domain {0}{1}.
setup.nodomain: This PC does not belong to a domain (or this is not the Windows app). A tenant without AD (cloud only) works too; otherwise fill in the domain controller under Connections.
setup.exchange: Exchange uses the same sign-in as the app (permission Exchange.Manage). You check the module ExchangeOnlineManagement under Check of this PC.
mailbox-detail.nogroup: There is no access group. By the agreement it is called {0}.
user-detail.marked-rows-differ-between-a: Marked rows differ between AD and Entra (spaces at the start or end do not count).
user-detail.no-groups-that-exist-only: No groups that exist only in Exchange; mail groups from Entra are under the cloud groups.
user-detail.what-changed-in-this-account: What changed in this account according to the snapshots, with the changes through Moss365 next to it.
user-detail.no-snapshots-of-this-account: No snapshots of this account yet.
user-detail.put-back-as-it-was: Put back as it was then
user-detail.a-change-without-a-line: A change without a line of Moss365 next to it happened outside the app (or in another app).
set-up-tenant.you-are-looking-at-a: You are looking at a state from the past. Go back to now to set up the tenant.
set-up-tenant.microsoft-says-which-tenan: Microsoft says which tenant belongs to a domain; you do not need to be signed in for that.
set-up-tenant.sign-in-with-an-administra: Sign in with an administrator of this tenant (role Application Administrator or Global Administrator, once). The sign-in link appears at the top; the wizard uses Microsoft Graph PowerShell, since the app registration of Moss365 may not exist yet.
set-up-tenant.the-wizard-only-works-in: The wizard only works in the Windows app.
set-up-tenant.make-a-group-per-profile: Make a group per profile (GG-Moss365-...): who is in the group gets the profile
set-up-tenant.give-myself-the-profiles-a: Give myself the profiles Administrator and App management

advice.score.none: Not computed yet: check everything first.
advice.score.help: Computed by Moss365 itself, on this PC, from the last result of the checks below: OK counts fully, attention half, a problem not, and an accepted risk counts as handled. Checks that weigh more (admin roles, MFA, AD) count more; the alerts do not count. Unlike Microsoft Secure Score, it also sees Active Directory.
advice.exception.help: An accepted risk no longer counts as attention or problem until that date (at most a year); then the advice comes back. Write down why, for example the agreement with the owner: it goes to the change log, as evidence for an audit.
advice.until-range: Choose a date from today to at most a year from now.
advice.not-allowed: You may not accept or lift risks.
advice.meldingen.what: Compares the organisation now with an earlier snapshot: new members of privileged groups and admin roles, disabled accounts that were enabled again, and changed Conditional Access policies, also when the change was made outside Moss365.
advice.meldingen.why: Whoever breaks in makes themselves admin, wakes up an old account or weakens a policy, so that they can come back. Such changes are rare, so each one deserves a look.
advice.meldingen.fix: Check every line: was it planned, and who did it? The change log shows whether it came from Moss365. Undo what nobody can explain, and reset the password of the account involved.
advice.meldingen.risk: This check changes nothing. Undoing a change that was planned after all can stop someone's work: ask first.
advice.doorsturen.what: Mailboxes and inbox rules that forward mail to an address outside your own domains.
advice.doorsturen.why: A forwarding rule is the classic sign of a taken-over mailbox: the attacker quietly gets a copy of every mail. It also leaks data when someone forwards work mail to a private address.
advice.doorsturen.fix: Remove forwarding that nobody needs, and block automatic forwarding to outside in the outbound spam policy, with an exception only for what is agreed.
advice.doorsturen.risk: A partner or a service may need its forwarding: removing it stops their mail. Check with the owner of the mailbox first.
advice.app-geheimen.what: Secrets and certificates of app registrations that expired or expire within 30 days.
advice.app-geheimen.why: An expired secret stops an integration (an HR link, a scanner, a backup) without warning. Long-lived secrets are a risk too: whoever finds one acts as the app, and attackers add their own secret to an existing app.
advice.app-geheimen.fix: Renew the secret or certificate in time, at the supplier or in the app, then remove the old one. Prefer certificates or managed identities to secrets, with a short lifetime.
advice.app-geheimen.risk: Removing a secret that is still in use breaks the integration at once: put the new one in place, check that the app works, then remove the old one.
advice.app-rechten.what: Apps with application permissions on everything (such as Mail.ReadWrite or Directory.ReadWrite.All), and apps that users gave consent to themselves.
advice.app-rechten.why: An app with application permissions needs no signed-in user and reaches every mailbox or file. A user who consents to a malicious app hands it their data (illicit consent).
advice.app-rechten.fix: Remove permissions and apps that are not needed, and let users ask for consent instead of giving it (the admin consent workflow), limited to verified publishers.
advice.app-rechten.risk: An app without its permission stops working: ask the owner of the app what it really needs before you remove anything.
advice.secure-score.what: Microsoft's own score for the security settings of Microsoft 365, with its trend and the actions that gain the most points.
advice.secure-score.why: One number to follow over time, also for management. The actions show what Microsoft sees as the biggest gaps, but without Defender for Identity it does not see Active Directory.
advice.secure-score.fix: Start with the actions worth the most points that fit your organisation. The hardening score of Moss365 also covers Active Directory.
advice.secure-score.risk: Not every action fits every organisation: some need a licence or change how people work. Read the action at Microsoft before you turn it on.
advice.rollen.what: Who has an admin role in Entra, permanently or only when activated (eligible, with Privileged Identity Management).
advice.rollen.why: Every permanent admin is a target: one stolen password or session gives the whole tenant. Microsoft advises fewer than five Global Administrators, and roles only when they are needed.
advice.rollen.fix: Remove roles nobody uses, give the smallest role that does the job, make the rest eligible with PIM (Entra ID P2), and use separate cloud-only admin accounts with phishing-resistant MFA.
advice.rollen.risk: Always keep at least two emergency accounts with Global Administrator that Conditional Access excludes, so that you never lock yourself out.
advice.zwakke-mfa.what: Accounts that have no MFA method, or only SMS, a phone call or e-mail.
advice.zwakke-mfa.why: SMS and calls can be intercepted or taken over with a SIM swap, and phishing kits pass them on in real time. Without MFA, one leaked password is enough.
advice.zwakke-mfa.fix: Have these people register Microsoft Authenticator or a passkey, then turn off SMS and voice in the authentication methods policy. Start with the administrators.
advice.zwakke-mfa.risk: Whoever has no other method yet can no longer sign in once SMS is off: give them a Temporary Access Pass to register a new method.
advice.risico.what: Users that Entra ID Protection marks as at risk or confirmed compromised (needs Entra ID P2).
advice.risico.why: Microsoft sees leaked passwords, sign-ins from unusual places and known attack patterns. An open risk can mean that someone else is using the account right now.
advice.risico.fix: Look at the sign-ins of the account. If it was not the user: block it, reset the password, revoke the sessions and check the inbox rules and MFA methods; then confirm or dismiss the risk.

advice.ad-beveiliging.what: What an attacker looks for first in Active Directory: user accounts with an SPN, unconstrained delegation, Kerberos pre-authentication off, 'password not required', reversible encryption, adminCount leftovers, outdated systems, an old krbtgt password, computers without LAPS, a machine account quota above 0 and the AD Recycle Bin off.
advice.ad-beveiliging.why: Accounts with an SPN can be cracked offline (Kerberoasting); unconstrained delegation lets a server act as anyone; an old krbtgt key keeps forged tickets (golden tickets) valid.
advice.ad-beveiliging.fix: Use gMSAs or long random passwords and AES only for service accounts, replace unconstrained delegation with constrained delegation (guided, one account at a time), clear the flags and the adminCount leftovers, set the machine account quota to 0, turn the Recycle Bin on, set up LAPS, retire outdated systems, and reset krbtgt twice a year in two rounds (with the library script).
advice.ad-beveiliging.risk: Changing a service account or a delegation can stop the service that uses it, and resetting krbtgt too fast breaks sign-ins: work in steps and check the replication in between.
advice.gpo.what: Group Policy objects that are linked nowhere, empty, or completely disabled.
advice.gpo.why: Unused policies make it hard to see what really applies, and a forgotten policy that someone can still edit is a way to run code on many PCs at once.
advice.gpo.fix: Remove or archive what is not used (back up the GPO first), and check who may edit the policies that remain.
advice.gpo.risk: A policy that is linked nowhere may be meant for later or used in a test: check with its owner before you remove it.

advice.exchange-instellingen.what: The settings of Exchange Online an attacker uses: SMTP AUTH (sending with only a password), automatic forwarding to outside, no External tag, the audit log off, and no preset security policy.
advice.exchange-instellingen.why: SMTP AUTH skips MFA, so a stolen password sends phishing from your domain. A forwarding rule to outside is the first thing an attacker sets up in a mailbox. Without the audit log nobody can see afterwards what happened.
advice.exchange-instellingen.fix: Turn off SMTP AUTH (guided: whoever used it in 30 days keeps an exception until moved), no automatic forwarding to outside, the External tag on, the audit log on, and the Standard preset security policy on.
advice.exchange-instellingen.risk: A scanner or application that sends with SMTP AUTH stops without an exception; forwarding someone needs stops; the preset policies can quarantine mail your own policies let through.
advice.maildomeinen.what: Per own domain: SPF (which servers may send), DKIM (mail signed by Exchange) and DMARC (what a receiver does with mail that fails both).
advice.maildomeinen.why: Without them anyone can send mail as your domain (an invoice from 'the director'), and big mail providers deliver your own mail less often.
advice.maildomeinen.fix: SPF with include:spf.protection.outlook.com and -all; DKIM on in Exchange (a plan here, after the two CNAME records); DMARC first with p=none and reports, then quarantine or reject. The DNS records are made at your DNS provider.
advice.maildomeinen.risk: A strict SPF or DMARC stops mail of a service that sends in your name and is not in SPF (a newsletter, a ticket system): add those first, and start DMARC with p=none.
